title: A loop whose only work is a self-concatenation never stops at the memory limit.
text: `string $b = 'ab'; while (true) { $b = $b . $b; }` runs forever at a constant working set under `nvs run`, with or without `--request`, where the same loop with an `echo` in its body stops with the memory-limit `FATAL` after 26 doublings. The refused doubling is [`string::concat_onto`]'s refusal branch, which releases the left operand and answers the empty string, so every later iteration joins `""` to `""` and allocates nothing. [`budget::refuse`] raises `MEMORY_LIMIT` on the polled word and [`ctx::Ctx::memory_breach`] reads [`budget::refused`], so the back-edge poll should report it; why it does not — the word not armed for this context, the flag lowered before the poll, or the loop carrying no poll — is not checked. The fix is also owed to `tests/hostile/core/Request-Mount/prefix/01-an-empty-prefix-that-grows.nvs`, which carries this record's marker.
